title: All‑Hands rapid reassurance talking points (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
- Quick raw notes for CEO/CTO two‑minute reassurance at next all‑hands (15min slot).
- Not polished: talking points, likely Qs + crib answers, rehearsal notes and sprint of followups.

Context (one‑liner to remind self):
- Partial degradation of hosted inference in us‑west on 2026‑03‑04 (multi‑model routing bug + autoscaler miscoordination). Some customers saw elevated latency and throttling for 90–120 minutes during morning traffic spike. SLA impact: brief latency SLO breach for a small % of requests. Most traffic served via fallback model variants and cross‑region failover.

High‑level messaging (for CEO):
- What to say first: 
  - Quick acknowledgement: "Yesterday morning we experienced a service degradation affecting a subset of hosted API requests in US‑West. We take uptime seriously and moved quickly to mitigate."
  - Reassurance: "Traffic was routed to fallback models/regions and the vast majority of customers continued to receive responses; for affected requests we prioritized correctness over speed while we stabilized."
  - Accountability: "We own this — root cause analysis underway and we will share a clear postmortem and action plan by next Tuesday."

Key points to emphasize (3):
1) People did the right things fast — SRE + serving runtime team implemented mitigations within ~20 minutes.
2) Failover systems worked (fallback models + cross‑region) limiting customer impact.
3) We’re making concrete safeguards: immediate config guardrails, autoscaler patch, expanded chaos checks; will publish timeline.

Script (short, conversational):
- "Good afternoon — quick update: on Wednesday morning we saw a partial service degradation in US‑West. Our SRE and serving teams quickly enacted fallbacks and mitigations; most customers were unaffected. We are conducting a full root cause analysis and will publish a detailed postmortem along with the fixes and timeline by next Tuesday. I know reliability is table stakes — this is on us and we’re moving fast to prevent recurrence."

FAQ / anticipated tough Qs + crib answers:
Q: How many customers were affected?
A: Small percentage of requests (low single‑digit percent of host traffic); we have a list of customers we’re proactively contacting. (note: confirm final numbers from analytics before publishing).

Q: Did customer data leak or get corrupted?
A: No evidence of data leakage or corruption. Fallbacks prioritized correctness and we logged everything for the RCA. Security and privacy teams are looped in.

Q: Will this impact pricing or SLAs?
A: No immediate pricing changes. We will honor SLA credits where SLA goals were missed and are reviewing thresholds to ensure fairness.

Q: Why did autoscaler fail to prevent this?
A: Root cause: race condition between the autoscaler and model routing decisions under specific spike patterns; suggested fix is a coordination lock + conservative ramp thresholds. (technical appendix to be added to postmortem).

Q: When will customers get a full postmortem?
A: We’re targeting a public postmortem by EOD next Tuesday; internal draft by Friday EOD to leadership.

Open questions / things to lock before all‑hands:
- Final numbers on affected requests and impacted customer list (Analytics: Rowan).
- Legal review of wording re: "no evidence of leakage" (Marta).
- Confirm SLA credit policy and how we’ll communicate to billing (Finance ops).
- Decide whether to include brief demo of fallback routing in the deck or keep to words only — CTO preference? (ask Ethan).

Followups / immediate action items (owners):
- Collect traffic numbers + timeline: Rowan (due 2026‑03‑09 12:00 PT).
- Draft postmortem skeleton for leadership review: Tara + Marta (due 2026‑03‑10).
- Draft customer outreach email for impacted customers: Customer Success (cc: Tara) (due 2026‑03‑11).
- Autoscaler hotfix PR and test plan: Serving Runtime (owner: Priyanka) (target merge 2026‑03‑12).
- Update chaos testbench to include routing+scaling interop scenario: Eng‑SRE (target 2026‑03‑20).

Slack/email blurbs (rough drafts):
- All‑hands 2‑min spoken line (CEO): "Quick update on yesterday’s partial degradation — our teams mitigated quickly, we’ll publish a postmortem next week, and we’re taking concrete steps to reduce risk going forward."
- Internal slack announcement after talk: "Short update posted in #all‑hands — postmortem draft will be available in Confluence by Friday. If you worked on mitigation please drop 1–2 bullets in this thread for the RCA."
- Customer outreach subject line suggestion: "Update on brief service disruption on Mar 4 — what we did and next steps"

Rehearsal notes (for CEO/CTO):
- Keep it < 90s. No technical deep dives on stage. Defer deep technical Qs to the postmortem and the CTO follow‑up session.
- Tone: calm, accountable, forward‑looking. Avoid jargon.
- If pressed for details, offer a single technical anchor (race condition between autoscaler and router) and redirect to postmortem.

Risky phrasing to avoid:
- "No customers were impacted" (inaccurate).
- "We fixed it permanently" (we’re patching; prefer "we’ve implemented mitigations and a plan to prevent recurrence").

Appendix (notes to self):
- Ticket list: INC‑3421 (primary), PRs: serving/patch/auto‑coord (WIP), linear task ids: LRN‑2215.
- Confluence draft link placeholder — will attach once internal review done.
- Reminder: update the all‑hands deck slide 4 (incidents/ops) with 2‑line summary + link to postmortem.

Quick checklist before sending to CEO for signoff:
- [ ] Confirm numbers (Rowan)
- [ ] Legal ok wording (Marta)
- [ ] SLA/billing note approved (Finance)
- [ ] CTO comfortable with single sentence technical anchor

Random scratch ideas (brainstorm):
- Quick customer webinar for affected customers? maybe overkill.
- Small blog post walkthrough of how our fallback routing works (good signal).
- Add an internal "postmortem readout" slot in next TGIF to share learnings with eng org.

Notes to self: this doc is rough — will convert into two outputs: (A) two‑line CEO script + 1 para for the all‑hands slide; (B) an internal Confluence postmortem skeleton.

---
Last edits: pulled together after post‑mitigation retro on 2026‑03‑05. Updated with target dates 2026‑03‑10 to 2026‑03‑20.

(End of scratchpad)
